title: Interface with the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code

content.overview: Corporate insolvency resolution and liquidation for debt default are under the IBC, with the NCLT as adjudicating authority. Chapter XIX of the Companies Act is omitted.
content.glance: Corporate insolvency resolution and liquidation for debt default are under the IBC, with the NCLT as adjudicating authority. Chapter XIX of the Companies Act is omitted.
content.study: A financial or operational creditor, or the corporate applicant, may initiate the corporate insolvency resolution process. Admission imposes a moratorium and shifts management to the resolution professional. The Companies Act still governs pre-insolvency duties, fraud, and the surviving winding-up grounds in s. 271. Avoid treating s. 253 as current law.

caseLaw.name: Swiss Ribbons Pvt Ltd v Union of India
caseLaw.point: The Supreme Court upheld the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code. A debt default is resolved under the Code. Tribunal winding up under section 271 is a separate Companies Act route.
